::: {.eyebrow}
PhD Statistics · Austin, Texas
:::

::: {.lede}
I'm a PhD statistician recently graduated from Baylor University. Most of my 
training is in Bayesian methods and clinical trial estimands. My favorite part 
of the work is that it's collaborative: the interesting problems arrive from 
someone else, in someone else's language, and I get to use my statistical
background to help solve them.
:::

I defended my PhD in Statistics at Baylor University in July 2026, advised by
Dr. John W. Seaman Jr. My dissertation developed Bayesian methods for two stages
of drug development: analyzing composite strategy estimands in confirmatory
trials, and estimating drug exposure in preclinical studies where each animal
contributes only a single measurement.

Alongside the methodology, I have spent several years doing applied work.
I interned with AstraZeneca's Late Respiratory and Immunology statistics group,
giving me exposure to the real clinical trial process and its common problems. 
I have supported clinical research at Baylor Scott &amp; White Health, and I 
consulted through Baylor's Statistical Consulting Center on problems ranging 
from municipal infrastructure to public health. I work mainly in R, alongside 
SAS and Python.
